Fun experience
Mar 2025 • Business
I had the pleasure of attending a private cooking class for a corporate event, and it was an unforgettable experience. I was picked up on a bicycle and rode through the vibrant streets of the city to the market, to learn more about the ingredients used in Vietnamese cooking. The market tour was an eye-opening experience … with some rats running around!!

Afterward, I headed to the kitchen, where I got hands-on preparing delicious chicken noodle soup and crispy Vietnamese pancakes. The it was time to taste the dishes I had just crafted, all while learning the techniques behind each recipe. It was a thrilling, educational, and truly memorable adventure.

There was only one other diner when I was there - a guy from Athens. The waitress spoke a little English and was very pleasant.

The main oddity of this place is that the walls are covered in graffiti left by (non-Vietnamese) guests and I was duly given a marker pen to add my own permanent thanks for a pleasant meal.

Sometimes I think that Trip Advisor reviews are self-perpetuating: rave reviews beget more rave reviews because people get caught up in the hype. Case in point: Cyclo Resto.

Considering they also run a cooking class, I expected more complexity and subtlety of flavour. 

The spring roll starter was like a panko-crusted popper. Shrimp, pork and carrot interior, but the bread crumbs killed it. Too much. 

The melon soup was excellent. A lovely combination with the melon providing a floral sweetness to the broth and crumbled pork adding savoury notes. Very well done. 

I wish the rest of the dishes lived up to the soup, but they didn’t. 

The fish, beans/pork and chicken were all fairly simple dishes that lacked subtlety and instead turned up the heat. I have no problem with spice when it’s there to enhance flavour, but all three of these dishes had hot peppery heat for heat’s sake. Also, the chicken was over cooked and the beans were limp.

Look, to each their own. Obviously many people love the food at Cyclo. The people around us seemed to be having a splendid time. But I also think people shouldn’t jump so quickly on bandwagons and instead pay more critical attention to what they’re actually eating.

First course was spring rolls - claimed to be the best in the world. They were very good.

Third course was 3 main dishes - 1 chicken, 1 pork and green bean and 1 fish. The fish was cooked in a clay pot and gave off some amazing flavours and smells. We went for this restaurant based on the huge number of fantastic reviews we saw on tripadvisor. The service was definitely top notch, with a homely feeling to it as described. However, we were underwhelmed by the food offered - plus the food is definitely very expensive by HCM standards. 135k vnd each, while you can get much better food at lesser than 100k vnd each at equivalent or better Vietnamese restaurants. 

This restaurant is more suitable for non-asians, who have not experienced asian food. For those well-acquainted to asian food, you will definitely not like the food there.

Their rice wine and fried spring rolls were good. Fish and chicken were just average, and portions were small for the price.

The melon soup was terrible. One taste and i could tell that the soup base came for instant noodles powder, full of MSG, with no effort made to brew soup from fresh ingredients. Felt thirsty after a few sips of the soup, and gave up on it. Elsewhere in HCM, most of their soup is brewed.

Lastly, the largest plate - stir fried long bean with pork. They gave a lot, probably because these are the cheapest ingredients there. Average as well. You can very easily get a much tastier and nicer version of this everywhere.

Dessert was simply cut pineapples.

Overall, if you are someone well acquainted with asian food - don't bother. You'll feel like you've been ripped off for average food. Their targeted audience would be non-asians, who trust TripAdvisor a lot, and I think they are very successful with this strategy.

That place was very busy that night. The manager had to turn a lot of people way since he didn't have enough room for them all. 

On the white walls of the restaurant he provides makers for the guest to write there own comments onto the walls. I read comments from travelers from all over the world there.

This would of been just another nice restaurant on my travels except for the fact that while I was walking to the restaurant my sandal broke on the walk over. I asked if the manager if he had any tape so I could do a quick patch up job to get me back to the hotel after. He said that he could fix it, thinking that he had some tape. Cyclo Resto is a restaurant serving westernized Vietnamese food to foreigners. If you have a hard time deciding or are scared to eat where locals eat, this is a good option for you. The restaurant has a very simple concept and comes with a 5 course meal for 120,000 Dong (about $6). 

We were underwhelmed by the food on average, but there were some hits and misses. I'll summarize since it's always the same:
1) "Spring rolls": I put this in quotes as these were closer to a previously-frozen and deep-fried jalapeno popper than any spring roll I've ever seen. Pretty gross...didn't finish them.
2) Winter melon soup: This soup was actually quite good and unique. Probably not everyone's cup of tea, but this was the one definite hit of the meal.
3) Stir-fried vegetables (with pork): You can find this one from Panda express in your local shopping mall...oily vegetables with bits of meat.
4) The double course...chicken with lemongrass and fish in clay pot: The chicken with lemongrass was fairly tasty and my second favorite dish...it's lots of lemongrass, so I hope you like it. The fish in clay pot was very challenging to eat with tons and tons of tiny bones. The flavor was sub-par, so we just decided to mess with it and left it uneaten.
5) Dessert: fruit that's cut up. You can't screw this one up. 

The restaurant itself was pretty basic. It's set on a noisy, unappealing alley way, and is rather hot and stuffy. Service was acceptable but nothing special. You are welcomed with a shot of some sort of homemade rocket fuel-like vodka. It's poured out of a plastic bottle...tastes about like alcoholic plastic.

Overall, if you'd like fairly cheap, average to below average Vietnamese food consumed in a room with other foreigners, this is your place. I just don't get the buzz.

Good idea and terrific service let down by the food.
Nov 2013 • Friends
A Vietnamese friend and I had lunch here yesterday. Our conclusion was that everything was right about this place - cooking classes in the restaurant, an exceptionally warm and friendly welcome and great service throughout. Everything, that is, except for the food.

Unfortunately the food served (with the exception of the excellent winter melon soup) was not typically Vietnamese and not even very good, although it was freshly cooked. A limited choice of the most common and basic Vietnamese dishes were offered, but the ones we had were mostly designed to cater to the taste of foreign tourists, and were therefore neither cooked nor presented in a typically Vietnamese way. That would have been OK if the dishes were an inspired improvement on the traditional recipes, but that was not the case. 

The spring rolls were covered in breadcrumbs and the interior had neither the consistency nor the taste of genuine Vietnamese spring rolls, which are so much better. Instead of being served with fresh leaves (sometimes lettuce) and fish sauce, they came without any greenery and were accompanied with a kind of marie rose sauce, which is not at all Vietnamese. We were told by the outstanding young waitress/manageress that many foreigners did not like nuoc mam (fish sauce), and so they offered this bland marie rose type of sauce instead. At least we should have been given the choice of eating the real thing rather than having this decision taken for us, but then the spring rolls themselves were not the real deal, so perhaps it didn't matter.

The chicken lemon grass had more of a taste of curry than anything else - no chilli or onion or garlic visible and hardly any taste of lemon grass. In Vietnam this dish is rarely composed of boneless chicken, as it was presented here. Again it was rather bland and not the genuine article. And the stir fried vegetables (mostly green beans) were much too sweet, even for the south Vietnamese. 

It would not matter so much if the restaurant did not advertise itself as serving and teaching typical Vietnamese cuisine. My Vietnamese friend was horrified at all the remarks on the wall written by tourists exclaiming that this was the best Vietnamese food ever. She felt that they had been misled, and gone away with a completely false impression of Vietnamese cooking. 

Clearly this place has many fans; so by all means give it a try. You will be extremely well looked after. You may enjoy the food a little or a lot, but don't leave the place believing that you have had a taste of the real Viet Nam. You haven't. For us the only two parts of our meal that were genuinely Vietnamese were the melon soup and the green tea - both excellent. And the service we received could not have been bettered.

And he did. 5 courses, all of them excellent. Great variety, we had prawns, chicken, beef, rice, soup, fruit, omelettes.. You name it. We weren't disappointed with any of it.

The decor in the place is really interesting too. You go upstairs, and there are 2 tables on a balcony, and then inside there is 1 long table where everyone sits. Its actually very nice, because its a great way to meet other people (although when we were there there was only a few other people, so this didnt really happen). The walls are covered in written reviews and messages that people have done in marker. Its done very well, not just graffiti and its nice to see what people have to say.

They also offer a cooking course, where they pick you up from your hotel, take you to the markets to buy fresh ingredients, and then you spend the day learning how to cook great vietnamese food. We will be doing this when we go back to HCMC!!

The place can be a little hard to find, but it is really excellent, and you will not be let down!

And remember to ask for a marker pen, to leave your mark :).

Cyclo has a small sign in front and is up a narrow and winding stair case opposite a large spa and salon sign.

The set course menu was a triumph of local cuisine, and we struggled to finish the meal. The owner and kitchen staff take great pride in the food and deserve to be proud of the results. Yes it's local, rustic and off the beaten track but well worth a visit. To get a cab back, walk up Dang Tran Con to Ly Tu Trong and there are plenty on that corner. If you are usually confined to District 1, this is an opportunity to visit the back packer area (Pham Ngu Lau Area). Just get a cab to Little Queenies, 12 Do Quang Dau. It's about 5 minutes from Cyclo Resto. Lots of funky little bars in this street and around the corner you will find interesting boutique clothing stores and street art galleries.
Took five trips to Saigon to discover this place and we will be back. To the owner Lê Ngọc Ân ..... you are a champion!
